false_assumption.statement: Gregory Ballaston murdered Ralph Endacott to gain the treasure.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Gregory had motive due to financial desperation and was found with one of the Images; he had suspicious behavior and was seen near the crime scene. The police and witnesses believed his key was used to enter the study.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It hides the fact that Ralph Endacott committed suicide and that Henry Ballaston was the actual murderer who staged the burglary and false accusation.

mechanism_description: Ralph Endacott committed suicide after translating the manuscript revealing the treasure's location. Henry Ballaston, motivated by control and family interests, confessed to the burglary and initially to the murder to protect Gregory. The treasure was hidden inside the two Images, which were reunited and opened to reveal the jewels.

discriminating_test.design: The test involves reenacting the opening of the two Images using the instructions found in the manuscript and letter. The Images are manipulated by pressing the eyes and ears in sequence to reveal hidden compartments and jewels. This reenactment proves the existence of the treasure and confirms the authenticity of the manuscripts.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The test reveals the mechanism to open the Images and the presence of the treasure inside, confirming the manuscript's instructions and the letter's truth.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Successful opening of both Images and discovery of jewels inside without damage.
